title: Vettem, vettél, vett...: The Full Past of vesz

sections.title: One irregular stem, regular endings
sections.content: vesz swaps its present stem vesz- for the irregular past stem vett- and then takes exactly the personal endings you already know from regular verbs — nothing else about it is special. The indefinite row answers "what did you buy (something)"; the definite row answers "what did you buy it/them (that specific thing)", almost always paired with meg-.

items.english: What did you buy at the store?
I bought a beautiful vase for Ildikó.
She caught sight of the vase, and bought it.

sections.content: felvesz ("to put on") and megvesz ("to buy up, buy the specific one") both run on this same vett- stem — felvettem a kabátot, megvettem a kabátot. Learn the stem once and every prefixed cousin of vesz falls into place.
